**▶ Online: https://radoslawo81.github.io/WebSpectrometer/** (Chrome / Edge, no installation)

First release of this fork of [jayden-sudo/WebSpectrometer](https://github.com/jayden-sudo/WebSpectrometer) (itself a browser port of Theremino Spectrometer). Everything runs locally in the browser.

### New in this fork / Nowości

**Measurement**
- **FWHM** – full width at half maximum of the peaks
- **Compare** – reference vs. second source: % change of the whole spectrum and of the UV / B / G / R / IR bands, shape difference
- **Light quality** (always-visible panel + detail window) – CCT, Duv, x/y, CRI Ra and R1–R14, luminous efficacy of radiation (LER), illuminance in lux, cd, lx/W
- **Spectral response calibration** from a halogen lamp (Planck), **"Corrected"** toggle applies it to the graph and saved files
- **Transmission** (glasses, filters, windows) – τv, sunglass category, UV/HEV/IR blocking, energy blocked per band, colour rendering through the lens
- **Absorbance (cuvette)** – A(λ), λmax, concentration via Beer–Lambert or a calibration line of standards
- **Time log** – total / band / single-wavelength intensity, peak position, CCT, lux over time, chart and CSV
- **HDR** – merge a short and a long exposure into one spectrum

**Calibration & lines**
- **Automatic wavelength calibration** from a reference lamp: CFL, UVC Hg/Ar, Ne, Na, H, He or sunlight (Fraunhofer lines)
- **Spectral lines** – reference-line overlay, automatic peak identification, 2nd-order diffraction zone and 2λ markers
- Ready calibration files (4-point CFL, 10-point Hg/Ar)

**Usability**
- **Saturation warning** – clipped regions marked red on the spectrum
- **Measurement report** – HTML with graph and all results, print to PDF
- **Polish language** (added alongside the existing ones; English and Polish complete)
- Modern scientific colour theme; Video input + Filters panels behind the **Camera & filters** button
- Camera list fix (shows all cameras, including USB spectrometers, after granting permission)

### Offline package
`WebSpectrometer-v1.0.0.zip` is the built site. Browsers do not run it from `file://`; unzip and serve the folder with any static server, e.g.:

```
cd WebSpectrometer-v1.0.0
python3 -m http.server 8000
```
then open http://localhost:8000 (camera access works on `localhost`).
